skeleton:
Black Pudding Eggs Benedict

British · Medium · Serves 2

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
Eggs Benedict walked into a greasy spoon and never left. This is the full English's answer to the brunch classic: thick slices of black pudding seared into crisp slabs that replace the muffin entirely, poached eggs (the foolproof poached master's method) riding on top, and a hollandaise made the café way — in the blender, in ninety seconds, unspillable. No English muffin, no ham: the black pudding is both bread-substitute and meat, and the plate is richer and darker for it. The blender hollandaise is the recipe's real gift. The whisked version has broken more Sunday mornings than any other sauce in the canon; the blender version is functionally unbreakable — the yolks whirl while hot butter streams in, and the emulsion forms itself. Learn it here and the bubble-and-squeak benedict, the salmon benedict, and every eggs Florentine afterwards are twenty-minute dishes.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The black pudding bases

  • thick enough to stand as a base, not a garnish

The poached eggs

The blender hollandaise

To finish

- **Mise en place is the whole game** — this plate has four moving parts (pudding, eggs, sauce, plates) and they all want to land in the same 90 seconds. Black pudding sliced, blender on the counter, poaching water heating, plates warming at 100 °C before anything starts. - **The hollandaise's butter must be properly hot** — fully melted and just bubbling, about 70 °C. The blender's whirl cools it fast; hot butter keeps the sauce warm and emulsified. Melt it in a small pan or the microwave (60–90 seconds) just before the eggs go in. - **Poaching water at a bare simmer** — 80–85 °C, bubbles barely breaking the surface — per the poached eggs master. Vinegar in. Eggs cracked into cups.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • Black pudding: 2 cm slices, dark-crusted both faces, flat and holding.
  • Hollandaise: thick ribbon in the blender, no butter pool; warm at the plate, not congealed.
  • Eggs: 3 minutes, towel-drained, trimmed; yolks running on the cut.
  • Assembly: sauce over, chives on, tomato beside — inside 90 seconds of the eggs leaving the water.

Black Pudding Eggs Benedict

Prep: 15 minutes · Cook: 15 minutes · Total: 30 minutes · Serves 2

Ingredients

The black pudding bases

  • 4 thick slices (300 g) good black pudding, 2 cm thick — thick enough to stand as a base, not a garnish

The poached eggs

  • 4 large eggs (220 g), as fresh as you can get
  • 2 litres water
  • 30 ml white wine vinegar

The blender hollandaise

  • 3 large egg yolks (55 g)
  • 5 ml lemon juice (about ½ lemon), plus more to taste
  • 5 ml water
  • 125 g unsalted butter
  • 1 g cayenne pepper
  • 2 g fine sea salt

To finish

  • 10 g chives, finely snipped
  • Freshly cracked black pepper
  • Grilled tomato halves (optional, for relief)

Instructions

  1. **Sear the black pudding bases, 6–7 minutes.** Heat a dry non-stick pan over medium heat (good black pudding renders its own fat; add a drop of oil only if yours is lean). Lay in the slices and cook 3 minutes a side, pressing gently with the spatula once to keep them flat, until both faces are dark-crusted and the middles are warmed through. Checkpoint — each slice is a firm, flat, dark slab that holds its shape under a gentle press — crisp enough to carry an egg, still slightly giving in the centre. If the middle is cold, 1 more minute a side at lower heat; if the edges are crumbling, the slices were cut thin — 2 cm is the floor.
  2. **Start the hollandaise while the pudding sears.** Put the yolks, lemon juice, water, salt, and cayenne in the blender jug. Melt the butter until fully liquid and just bubbling. When the pudding is turned to its second side, run the blender on high for 20 seconds to warm and whip the yolks, then — with the motor running — pour the hot butter in a thin, steady stream through the lid's hole over about 20 seconds. The sauce thickens visibly as the last of the butter goes in. Stop, taste, adjust lemon and salt. Checkpoint — the sauce is thick, glossy, and pale yellow — it coats the blender blade and falls in a slow ribbon. A spoonful held up shows no separated butter pool on top. If it looks thin, blend 10 more seconds; the emulsion tightens as it whips.
  3. **Poach the eggs, 3 minutes.** Slide the eggs from their cups into the barely-simmering water and poach 3 minutes for set whites and liquid yolks — 2½ minutes if your yolks are small, 3½ for very large. Lift with a slotted spoon, drain 3 seconds on a folded tea towel or kitchen paper, and trim any straggly white with the spoon's edge. Checkpoint — each egg's white is fully set around a yolk that domes and wobbles when nudged. The towel-drain matters — a wet egg slides off its pudding base and waters the hollandaise.
  4. **Land hot, in order.** Black pudding slab, egg on top, hollandaise spooned over generously — the sauce should run down the pudding's sides and pool slightly on the plate — then chives, black pepper, and the tomato alongside for relief. Checkpoint — the first cut through the egg lets the yolk run into the hollandaise, and the eating order is sauce-egg-pudding in one bite: dark, rich, sharp, hot. Everything at once and everything warm — the plate's whole test.

Finish & Plate

Two plates, the benedict at the centre, grilled tomato for acid relief, and — the fry-up's honest addition — a forkful of the bubble-and-squeak cakes if yesterday's mash exists, because this plate and that cake were made for each other. Coffee or builder's tea; brown sauce stays in the cupboard for once, because the hollandaise has claimed the plate.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Hollandaise split or butter poolingButter poured too fast, or butter not hot enough1 tbsp hot water + 15 seconds' blending re-forms it; next time, thinner stream
Hollandaise congealed by platingMade too earlyIt holds 20 minutes in the blender jug in a warm (not hot) water bath; re-whip 5 seconds before serving
Eggs broke in the waterToo-fresh handled or violent simmerBare simmer, cup-to-water slide, 3 minutes — the poached master's method
Black pudding crumbledSlices under 2 cm, or pressed too hardThick slices, one gentle press only
Plate arrived coldNo mise en place or cold platesWarm plates, four parts rehearsed, the 90-second landing window respected

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **Hollandaise holds 20 minutes** in a warm water bath and cannot be revived from the fridge — make what you eat. Black pudding sears ahead fine (refrigerate 3 days, re-sear 2 minutes). Eggs always fresh. - **Variation — bubble-and-squeak eggs benedict:** the sibling record — mini bubble cakes under the egg, same hollandaise, the leftover-economy version of this plate. - **Variation — the full fry-up benedict:** a rasher of back bacon between pudding and egg — the ham slot filled, the plate now a full English in benedict's clothing. - **The scaling note:** the blender hollandaise doubles perfectly (6 yolks, 250 g butter) — four benedicts, one jug, no extra time.
